chunks: Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, Mu‘āwiyah ibn ‘Ammār, ‘Abd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, and al-Ḥalabī all narrated from Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

When you perform salat in Masjid al-Shajarah, then say—while you are seated at the end of the salat, before you stand—the words that the muhrim says. Then stand and walk until you reach the mile marker and al-Baydā’ levels out with you. Then when al-Baydā’ has leveled out with you, recite the talbiyah.

key_terms.الْبَيْدَاءُ: al-Bayda’, the flat open terrain mentioned as the point for talbiyah
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: the one who has entered the state of ihram
key_terms.الْمِيلَ: the mile marker used here as a point of travel reference
key_terms.دُبُرِ الصَّلَاةِ: the conclusion or immediate aftermath of the salat
key_terms.فَلَبِّ: recite the talbiyah; proclaim the pilgrim's response
key_terms.مَسْجِدِ الشَّجَرَةِ: Masjid al-Shajarah, the miqat location where ihram is initiated

ai.seo_question: When should a pilgrim recite the talbiyah after praying at Masjid al-Shajarah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal instruction concerning the procedure of entering ihram from Masjid al-Shajarah. It specifies that the muhrim's words are said after salat while seated, and that the talbiyah is to be recited upon reaching al-Baydā’, making it an important narration in the fiqh of hajj.
